title: A chart engine that refuses text-alternative access is refused on the applying project
asA: shelf reviewer gating an applying project's chart engine choice
iWant: the blueprint to refuse a chart engine choice that renders canvas-only surfaces with no text-alternative path
soThat: the text-alternative REQ-003 and the keyboard-traversal REQ-004 stay reachable through the render shell's contract regardless of the chosen engine (ADR-1901)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given ADR-1901's engine choice, one of the canonical tokens `recharts`, `echarts`, `chart-js`, `d3-primitives` or `hand-authored-svg` on `blueprint.json:elicits[].chart-engine.options` (the manifest owns the token set; every other layer references these tokens verbatim), the applying project's manifest records the engine and the text-alternative reach: the engine's rendered chart is paired with a `<table>` element the pack asserts (AC-18103-1). An engine that renders exclusively to a `<canvas>` and does not offer a text-alternative surface is refused at project-side review; the refusal is documented in the blueprint's README under the engine-refusal rule. Applying agent sets: the `blueprint.json:elicits[].chart-engine.options` token (one of `recharts`, `echarts`, `chart-js`, `d3-primitives`, `hand-authored-svg`) recorded on the manifest, and the paired `<table>` mount the pack asserts under AC-18103-1.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the applying project's chart mount is reviewed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the engine is refused if it renders canvas-only surfaces with no text-alternative path

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a compliant engine choice, the applying project's rendered chart carries the `data-chart-engine` attribute whose value equals the canonical engine token elicited on `blueprint.json:elicits[chart-engine]` (`recharts`, `echarts`, `chart-js`, `d3-primitives` or `hand-authored-svg`). This is a project-side observation, not a pack check; the README names it under known mechanism-reach gaps as a documentation contract on the applying project. Applying agent sets: the value elicited on `blueprint.json:elicits[chart-engine]` (one of the five canonical tokens). The `data-chart-engine` attribute name is fixed on TAC-1901-application-charts-render-shell.responsibilities[6].
acceptanceCriteria.given: a compliant chart engine on the applying project
acceptanceCriteria.then: the engine name is discoverable on the rendered DOM through a stable attribute

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the applying project mounts a chart whose engine renders exclusively to a `<canvas>` and offers no text-alternative surface, when the shell factory attempts to mount, then the mount is refused before any DOM is produced and no `<canvas>` element attaches to the target root. Applying agent sets: the applying project's engine choice that fails the text-alternative check (a canvas-only engine with no text-alternative surface). The refusal-record shape written on refusal is fixed on TAC-1901-application-charts-render-shell.responsibilities[5].
acceptanceCriteria.given: an engine choice whose runtime provides no text-alternative surface
acceptanceCriteria.when: the shell attempts to mount a chart on the applying project's surface
acceptanceCriteria.then: the mount is refused before DOM attachment and no chart element renders

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a refused mount as observed in AC-18106-3, the render log matches the refusal-record shape fixed on TAC-1901-application-charts-render-shell.responsibilities[5]: exactly one warning entry per refused chart declaration is present and a re-mount with a compliant engine attaches DOM without re-warning.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a text-alternative refusal has fired once for a given chart declaration
acceptanceCriteria.then: the render log matches the refusal-record shape fixed on TAC-1901.responsibilities[5] and re-mount with a compliant engine attaches DOM without re-warning
